component.name: Loft
component.summary: Desktop integration for messaging apps on Linux

description.p: Loft gives your favourite messaging web apps a proper place on your Linux desktop. WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, Slack, Telegram, Element (Matrix), and NextCloud Talk each run in their own dedicated window — with full voice and video calling, system tray icons, unread badge counts, desktop notifications, and close-to-tray behaviour.
Loft integrates natively with both GNOME and KDE Plasma: window show/hide and focus, panel or tray icons with per-service Do Not Disturb, and notifications that take you straight to the conversation.

description.p: Bubbles have landed. Any chat, channel or room you keep coming back to can now live below your services as its own round button, showing that person's or group's picture with a small badge for the service it came from. Clicking it takes you straight there — waking the service first if it was asleep, and finding the conversation even when it has scrolled out of a long list. Pin from the titlebar's pin button, or by right-clicking a service in the rail. Works across WhatsApp, Messenger, Slack, Telegram, Element and NextCloud Talk.

ul.li: Signing back in to Messenger no longer throws you out to your web browser. The button that approves the login now stays in Loft, where it can actually finish.
Loft now notices when your whole system is set to Do Not Disturb on GNOME, so notifications stop arriving with it switched on. This needs the Loft GNOME extension installed and up to date.
Do Not Disturb is picked up on far more desktops. Loft used to look for it only on KDE.
The tray icon now appears on KDE and other desktops. GNOME was never affected, as it uses the Loft GNOME extension's panel button instead.
Element notifications now show the sender's picture.

description.p: A same-day fix for Loft 1.0, which reported a crash every time you logged out.

ul.li: Logging out no longer leaves an "Electron crashed" report waiting at your next login. Loft now tells GNOME it is part of the session and shuts down properly when the session ends. Your accounts and settings were never at risk — but the report appeared on every single logout.
Window sizes and positions are saved as you move and resize them, so they survive Loft being closed abruptly.
The Flatpak build now builds on FriendlyHub, and moves to the 25.08 runtime so it keeps getting system library and security updates.

description.p: Loft 1.0 is a complete rewrite. Google Chrome is no longer needed — Loft now brings everything with it — and your messaging lives together in one window instead of a separate one for every service.

ul.li: All your services in one window, with a sidebar to switch between them. Each has its own titlebar and unread count, and closing one tucks it away in the tray while it keeps running in the background. Prefer a service in its own window? Turn that on in its settings and Loft remembers.
New grid view: put several services on screen at once instead of switching back and forth. Drag services in, drag the dividers to resize them, and Loft brings the arrangement back next time.
Multiple accounts: sign in to two WhatsApps, two Slacks, or two NextCloud Talk servers, and give each one its own name and icon so you can tell them apart.
More say over what opens when: each service can stay closed, start quietly at login, or load only when you open Loft.
Calls, screen sharing, unread badges, panel and tray icons, Do Not Disturb, and notifications that take you straight to the message all work as before, with smoother GNOME and KDE Plasma integration.

description.p: One-time change: you'll need to sign in to each service again after upgrading.

ul.li: The service manager has a cleaner, less cluttered look that stays tidy as you add more services. Your installed services and the ones you can add now sit in separate sections, each installed service has its own Open and settings buttons, and the window sizes itself to fit.
The manager now shows which of your services are running and how many unread messages each has, updating live while the window is open.
Opening a service from the GNOME activities overview now takes you straight to its window, instead of leaving the overview open with the window hidden.
Loft services now keep their place in the GNOME Alt+Tab switcher — the one you just used stays at the front of the list.
Added support for Element (Matrix), including self-hosted instances, with unread badges and Do Not Disturb.
Added support for NextCloud Talk on your own NextCloud server, with unread badges and notifications that show the sender's avatar.
Loft now prompts you to log out and back in when it updates its GNOME integration, so window management keeps working.
Tray icons now appear when Loft is installed as a Flatpak. Previously the sandbox blocked the tray's standard D-Bus name, so nothing showed up in the panel.
The panel/tray icon now reliably shows up at login when multiple services autostart.
Hide-to-tray from the Loft titlebar now works when Loft and Chrome are both installed as Flatpaks.
Clicking a service from a different workspace brings its window to you, instead of showing a "ready" notification and throwing you back to the original workspace.
The dock now shows a proper icon for each service (Messenger, WhatsApp, Slack, Telegram) instead of a single Chrome icon. Alt-tabbing to a service also correctly raises its window.
Messenger notifications now include emoji that were part of the message.
The Loft titlebar slides in smoothly on Telegram instead of stuttering.
Links to Facebook itself (profiles, posts, photos…) inside a Messenger conversation now open in your default browser instead of replacing the conversation.
Logging out with Loft services running no longer produces "Chrome has crashed" notifications on your next login.
Loft now shows an unread count in GNOME's Background Apps list, so you can see at a glance how many messages are waiting without opening the app.
Desktop notifications now appear when a Loft window is open but not focused (for example, hidden behind another app). Previously they only appeared when the window was minimised or closed to tray.

description.p: Initial release with WhatsApp, Messenger, Slack and Telegram support.
